comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–2027 curriculum; Dutch part-time target, six-year recommended pacing
comparator.sourceNotes: The permanent target remains the Dutch part-time offering, not a separate English or full-time degree. Annex 1 supplies the selected comparative Religie en Levensbeschouwing route: ten 6-EC units in academic stage 1, ten 6-EC positions in stage 2, and 30-EC minor/profiling plus five 6-EC units in stage 3. Academic-stage totals are 60+60+60=180; the part-time table distributes these over six calendar years at 36,24,36,24,36,24 EC. The current route name is not conflated with the differently described Zingeving, geestelijke verzorging en samenleving programme starting in 2027. Article 10.4 specifies Dutch instruction in the first two academic stages, some English courses, and English instruction in the selected third stage; normalized instruction metadata includes NLD and ENG while raw Dutch provenance is retained. Four restricted positions are instantiated using the first-listed eligible alternative in each period, independently of UCR fit. Alternatives are not stacked. The 30-EC minor remains generic: Article 12.1 allows a qualifying minor or approved academic courses (at least 12 EC level 300), or placement up to 12 EC plus 18 EC courses; applicable approval, entry and non-overlap rules remain. The 0-EC Dutch test is embedded in Geschiedenis van de Wereldfilosofie, not added as credit. Research Lab: Preparation Thesis requires 120 EC, the analytic-methodologies lab follows participation in preparation, and the thesis follows completed preparation. Adopted current rules establish a pathway, not guaranteed future timetable availability. Re-audit 17 October 2026 reopens and confirms the adopted route/credits and part-time table directly. Current marketing redirects to a programme explicitly starting in 2027; it is not substituted for the 2026–2027 route. Article 9.1 additionally requires completion of all first-stage and first-semester second-stage units before preparation; its 120-EC threshold is not the sole condition. Current course-level pages independently checked for world philosophy, myth/ritual and Social Sciences. Social Sciences is substantive religion-focused theory, not a generic methods module; it remains unmatched.

alternatives.concept: Philosophy explores meaning, ethics and the self, while literature, myth and heritage examine how cultures express and interpret those questions. alternativeSelection.assessment: One complete broader response is justified by philosophical meaning, myth/text/image interpretation and belief in public life, with concrete complementary social, legal and qualitative methods study. The former no-match imposed an overly narrow all-religion-content test: it correctly identified specialist gaps, but those gaps do not invalidate this differently organised related-fields programme. Religion/political conflict would mostly relabel the same social/public-life strand; sustainability courses do not establish the religious-environment interaction needed for a separate religion-centred direction. Biblical/confessional and Islamic candidates require sustained source interpretation, theology and related languages that the documented UCR offerings cannot implement; generic humanities are not relabelled to fill them. These directions are independently considered, not excluded by the absence of a degree title or professional licence. One programme is retained; no second is manufactured.

notes.text: VU offers sustained study of religious traditions, religious experience, sacred-text interpretation and religion-specific research. The UCR programme connects philosophy, myth, heritage and social life; it does not reproduce that specialist sequence or confer theological, ministry or spiritual-care qualifications. VU’s required thesis differs from the separately displayed optional UCR research opportunity.

audience.programmeDescription: Theology and Religious Studies at VU Amsterdam examines religious traditions, beliefs, texts and practices, and their place in society. This comparison uses the 2026–2027 Religion and Worldviews route, which combines study of several traditions with philosophy, social perspectives and research. The selected offering is part-time.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers a broader combination of philosophy, myth, cultural interpretation and belief in public life. It does not reproduce VU’s sustained study of religious traditions, sacred texts and religion-specific research. Shared rows indicate limited content relationships; blank cells preserve important differences. The UCR programme is not professional training for ministry or spiritual care.
